mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in workplace and transit mobility at t-0w, coupled with a decrease in residential time, indicates a broader return to pre-pandemic routines, which will positively impact retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, or if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reverse their recent gains.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility at t-0w, following a period of decline, signals a turning point in consumer confidence and willingness to engage, driving further short-term gains over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the next two weeks despite the recent uptick observed at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and strong recovery in both workplace and transit station mobility at t-0w indicates a coordinated return to urban centers and commuting, creating a synergistic effect that will boost retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, or if the recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A general easing of public health restrictions, evidenced by the broad increase in out-of-home mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, WORKPLACES) and decrease in residential time at t-0w, will lead to a sustained increase in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: New public health restrictions are imposed, or the observed broad mobility trends reverse significantly over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in residential mobility at t-0w indicates a strong immediate shift away from staying at home, directly translating to increased out-of-home activities including retail and recreation in the very short term (next week).
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an immediate increase in the next week, or if RESIDENTIAL mobility rebounds significantly.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in transit station mobility exceeding 10 percentage points at t-0w signals a critical mass of people returning to public transport, which will drive a sustained increase in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 10 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility does not sustain its recovery, or if RETAIL_REC fails to improve despite the transit surge over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in both essential (grocery/pharmacy) and non-essential (retail/recreation) out-of-home activities at t-0w suggests a broad increase in public comfort and willingness to leave home, which will reinforce each other to drive further RETAIL_REC gains over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM or RETAIL_REC mobility declines in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: As spring progresses into early summer (mid-May), increasing outdoor activity, reflected in PARKS mobility, will indirectly encourage more general out-of-home movement, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks, assuming favorable weather conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point 2021-05-15 suggests seasonal shift
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains stagnant or declines, or if unseasonably bad weather occurs, preventing the expected increase in RETAIL_REC.
